best.plan_strategy: Attempt 1: replace the linear baseline with a gradient-boosted tree ensemble to raise the ranking itself, and move the operating point in the same fit. Fit hist_gbdt on all 29,304 training rows with impute: none so the estimator splits on NaN directly in workclass/occupation/native-country's one-hot encoding, no scaling, early_stopping disabled so the full training split is used, 400 boosting iterations at learning_rate 0.08, max_leaf_nodes 31, max_depth 8, l2_regularization 1.0, and class_weight 'balanced' to push recall up against specificity, since balanced_accuracy is their mean and the default cut on a 3.18:1 target sits far on the specificity side (baseline recall 0.6008). Then read roc_auc / balanced_accuracy_at_best_cut / cut_headroom: cut_headroom tells attempt 2 whether the remaining distance is on the ranking axis (needs more capacity or a different family) or on the operating point (needs an explicit weight map heavier than 'balanced').

Sizing the family swap honestly: only one family has been tried (hist_gbdt, max 0.8452), so there is no measured per-family span here, and the recorded sizes for a family swap elsewhere are 0.0022–0.0077 roc_auc — smaller than the 0.0380 of balanced_accuracy still needed, so a second family is the best available lever but is not guaranteed to close the gap on its own; with 4 iterations left it is worth one attempt before concluding the bar is out of reach for the columns as given (no feature derivation is available).
